newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia police ready for poll trouble.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia police ready for poll trouble.

text.p: Five thousand Indonesian police clashed in a mock riot on Wednesday to demonstrate their readiness to halt possible violence during the general election campaign, which officially begins on Sunday.
A number of police trainees, playing the part of rioters, received treatment for slight head wounds and other minor injuries after they were baton-charged and sprayed with water cannon.
Black smoke rose from burning car wrecks and tyres on a closed street to simulate riot conditions. A bomb was defused and hostages freed with force in the exercise.
"Just you put the message out. The Jakarta metropolitan police are ready," the region's police spokesman, Lieutenant-Colonel Edward Aritonang, told Reuters.
"We hope a situation like this will not happen, but if it does then we are ready," Aritonang said.
The government has banned parades and marches in a bid to prevent violence between political partisans during the election campaign leading up to the May 29 national and local polls.

Last July, central Jakarta was hit by two days of rioting in which five people died, a number of buildings were destroyed and cars burned after a police-backed raid on the headquarters of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) during an internal party dispute.
In the past month, Central Java province has been the scene of increasing politically linked violence ahead of the campaign.
